strict.criterion: Routine personal and business calls provide convincing three-dimensional physical presence via direct-eye or holographic displays.
strict.rationale: Ordinary calls in 2019 and 2026 remain audio or flat 2D video on screens. Direct-eye or holographic 3D calling is not part of everyday communications.
changedConditions: Enforces routine calling adoption and 3D direct-eye/holographic realism

evidence.title: HP: Dimension with Google Beam at InfoComm 2025
evidence.note: Enterprise light-field telepresence, six-camera capture. Launch/availability plan supports capability and commercialization, not routine calls or demonstrated above-human acuity.

reference.criterion: Routine calls offer three-dimensional physical-presence realism using the specified direct-eye or holographic display systems.
reference.rationale: Ordinary 2019 video calls did not deliver the asserted 3D physical-presence experience and acuity. Google Beam/HP Dimension demonstrates a serious enterprise 3D telepresence direction, but not routine consumer calls or proven above-human acuity.

broader.criterion: Convincing 3D light-field telepresence emerges commercially, even if confined to expensive specialist booths rather than routine calls.
broader.rationale: HP Dimension with Google Beam (announced June 2025) demonstrates genuinely convincing 3D light-field telepresence in an enterprise product, warranting partial credit. Treating a rare, specialized multi-camera conference booth as full realization of routine 3D calling overstates the outcome.
changedConditions: Credits enterprise light-field booths as partial without treating them as routine consumer calls
